attribution: EC Funded CAVIAR project / IST 2001 37540, University of Edinburgh; publicly released CC BY-SA footage and hand annotations.
selection: Highest directional event F1 on the three validation recordings; fewer false events breaks ties; then prefer calibrated pretrained model to training. No holdout outcomes until selected profile and source/code hashes are saved.
event_scoring: One-to-one predicted/reference events of same direction within 1.0 second. All annotated crossings are scored; no ambiguous-event exclusion. Also report per-direction totals and absolute errors, including pass-by-only negative clips.
reference_method: Manually review entrance crossings in source footage with published human track IDs and shop-enter/exit activity intervals. Store exact crossing frames and review notes before running any detector on that split. Trajectory line crossings are proposals for review, not automatic reference truth.
limitations: One indoor shopping-centre camera, older 384x288 footage, scripted activities; not proof for modern outdoor malls or night/weather performance.
Different complete takes are split; cameras, recording day and some actors are shared. This is a same-camera pilot, not a new-location generalization test.
Synchronized corridor camera copies are excluded from every split. Previous local benchmark footage is excluded.
Public pretrained model overlap with CAVIAR is unknown.
Few independent entrance events cannot establish a dependable 95% claim, even if sample scores exceed it.
Some stationary background people are not annotated; full-scene box accuracy is not an acceptance measure here. Every visible entrance crossing must be checked separately.
development_changes: After inspecting development labels/source only, widen deadband from 3 to 6 pixels to resist rail/box jitter on passing groups; no holdout detector outcomes inspected.
selection_revision: After validation and before holdout model outcomes: select highest identity-verified crossing F1 (same direction, <=3s timing difference, >=3 one-to-one IoU>=0.3 associations with published human IDs); fewer unverified events breaks ties, prefer pretrained on ties. Retain original one-second scores separately. Original rule and outcomes remain in the report.
